testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip, what should you see?

options.text: No part of your vehicle in any mirror.
Some part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
More than half of your vehicle in each mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: When you adjust your mirrors correctly, you should see some part of your own vehicle. This gives you a reference point to judge where other objects are.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tank completely.

questions.question: What should be done with cargo on a flatbed?

options.text: Heavy cargo does not need to be strapped down.
Do not strap it down if driving slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down. This prevents it from shifting or falling off during the trip.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth needed in every major groove of a front tire?
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When should cargo securement be checked after starting a trip?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo secure throughout the trip.

questions.question: What do the two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually say?
questions.explanation: Older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: What can affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on vehicle speed, weight, and road surface grip.

questions.question: While driving, what should a driver be aware of?

options.text: Only what is ahead, not the sides.
What is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Only what is ahead, not what is behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of all sides of your vehicle. Look ahead and check both mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When starting the engine, dashboard lights should come on and then turn off. If the yellow ABS light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the system is not working.

questions.question: When checking your tires, what should you NOT find?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch tread depth. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, what should you look at?
questions.explanation: Check that your tire pressure is not too low or too high before you drive.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles, the parking brake has a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle likely to tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: Look for an escape ramp first. If none is available, drive to a safe area like an open field or flat side road to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe to use if a professional did the repairs.
Safe to use if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims with welding repairs. Replace them before driving.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 2 psi of air in one minute during a static leakage test. Higher leakage means something needs repair.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have a leakage rate of no more than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: On long trips, you should:
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Do not drive when you would normally be sleeping.

questions.question: You should check and adjust your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture may change, so mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Should never be done the same way twice.
Should always be done in the same order.
Do not need to be done if you know the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do inspections in the same order every time. This helps you learn the steps and makes it less likely you will miss something.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle is okay until someone else drives it.
Check what is wrong and fix it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check what is wrong and fix it.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, get it checked right away.

questions.question: When backing up with a helper, where should the helper stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger's side.
In front of the driver's side.
Near the back of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The helper should stand near the back where the driver can see them. They can watch the blind spots and guide the driver safely.

questions.question: Which action helps you avoid distracted driving?
questions.explanation: Plan ahead to avoid distractions. Pre-program your radio, plan your route, adjust mirrors before driving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: If the previous driver left an inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Skip your own inspection and trust the report.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Always review any inspection report left by the previous driver as your first step.

questions.question: What happens when cargo is loaded too high?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
Items are more likely to fall.
It is harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Loading cargo too high increases the risk of a rollover. Distribute weight evenly and keep it low.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you can:
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder is often the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough for large vehicles.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: If workers are in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down below the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. If workers are present, drive even slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: On the basic control skills test, you lose points if you:
questions.explanation: Each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line, it counts as an error against your score.

questions.question: What happens if weight is not balanced evenly in a trailer?

options.text: It is harder to handle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder to handle safely.
questions.explanation: Unbalanced weight makes a vehicle difficult to steer and control. Distribute weight evenly from front to back and side to side, and keep it as low as possible.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand or foot on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during a driving test, always face the vehicle. Keep three points of contact with the vehicle at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: A cargo van with a heavy load will:

options.text: Be about the same height as when empty.
Be taller than when it is empty.
Sit lower than when it is empty.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit lower than when it is empty.
questions.explanation: Heavy loads make a vehicle sit lower. Light loads make a vehicle sit higher. A vehicle that fits under a bridge when fully loaded may not fit when empty.

questions.question: If ice forms on your side mirror:

options.text: You should pull off the road.
The road surface is likely icy.
The road will not be icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road surface is likely icy.
questions.explanation: If ice forms on your mirrors or wipers while driving, the road is probably icy too.

questions.question: You can only check mirror adjustment properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight hill.

questions.explanation: On vehicles with trailers, check mirror adjustment only when the trailers are straight. Check your mirrors before every trip.

questions.question: Before backing up, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk behind the vehicle to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind the vehicle to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk the area to look for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both side mirrors.

questions.question: The only way to sober up after drinking alcohol is to:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers and coffee do not speed this up. Time is the only thing that works.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, the posted speed:

options.text: Can be exceeded when passing another vehicle.
Can be exceeded in rural areas.

questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under good conditions. Always slow down when road or weather conditions require it. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Air tank drains should be:

options.text: Opened daily to empty the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened daily to empty the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks collect water and oil. These can damage the brakes. Open the drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Hydroplaning most often happens when:

options.text: A vehicle is going faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens most when tires are underinflated and the tread is worn on wet roads. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should turn on and then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn on and then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should come on when you start the engine, then turn off after a few seconds.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk around the area to see what's there.
Don't use both side mirrors because they distract you.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can learn from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around the area to see what's there.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and check your path. Look for obstacles on the sides and overhead.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different control sets.
One system for the left side of the truck and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear brakes, and the other controls the front brakes.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on surfaces with poor grip. On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: What can happen with improperly loaded cargo?

options.text: It looks bad to other drivers.
It can injure or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
It makes it easier to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can injure or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Loose or unsecured cargo is dangerous. During a sudden stop, cargo can fall and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: Except for the straight line backing test, how many times can you get out to check your vehicle during a test?
questions.explanation: You can get out to check your vehicle's position during tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can only look once. For other tests, you can look up to two times.

questions.question: If you have more than one driver's license, what could happen?

options.text: States share computer networks and you may get caught.

questions.correctAnswerText: States share computer networks and you may get caught.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent people from getting multiple licenses. It is illegal to have more than one driver's license.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if the pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: What should you do with a cracked rim?

options.text: Move it to one of the dual tires.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving for any damage. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the roadside, you must:
questions.explanation: If you stop on the roadside, you must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: When parking, when should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: After going down a steep hill, your brakes may be hot. Don't use the parking brake until they cool down, or you may damage them.
